s: The dismissal of N.T. Rama Rao's government in 1984 is a textbook example of the alleged misuse of whose discretion?
x: The 1984 dismissal is cited as a classic misuse of gubernatorial discretion and fed into the later Sarkaria Commission debates.

s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: N.G. Ranga – First President of the Andhra Socialist Party
Communist Party – Initiated the Visalandhra Movement
Marri Chenna Reddy – President of the Telangana Praja Samithi
Nadendla Bhaskara Rao – President of the Telangana Praja Samithi
x: Nadendla Bhaskara Rao formed the Democratic Telugu Desam Party; it was Marri Chenna Reddy who led the Telangana Praja Samithi.

s: Which Governor dismissed N.T. Rama Rao's government in August 1984?
x: Governor Ram Lal dismissed NTR while he was in the US; Nadendla Bhaskara Rao was sworn in and resigned on 16 September 1984.

s: Who was the first non-Congress Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh?
x: N.T. Rama Rao was the first non-Congress CM; Congress ruled uninterrupted from 1956 until 1983.

s: How many seats did the Telugu Desam Party win in the 1983 Andhra Pradesh Assembly election?
x: The TDP won 202 seats in 1983 and formed the first non-Congress government in AP.

s: Who among the following was the Deputy Chief Minister in N.T. Rama Rao’s initial cabinet?
x: Nadendla Bhaskara Rao served as Deputy Chief Minister in N.T. Rama Rao’s initial cabinet.

s: Which of the following about the 1984 political crisis in Andhra Pradesh is NOT correct?
o: Nadendla Bhaskara Rao was sworn in as Chief Minister on 16 August 1984
Indira Gandhi was assassinated on 31 October 1984
The mid-term polls were held before Indira Gandhi's assassination
N.T. Rama Rao was sworn in again on 9 March 1985
x: The mid-term polls were held on 28 December 1984, after Indira Gandhi's assassination on 31 October.

s: Neelam Sanjiva Reddy did not appoint a Deputy Chief Minister. How did he describe the post?
x: Neelam Sanjiva Reddy appointed no Deputy CM, calling the post a 'sixth finger'.

s: Through which Constitutional Amendment was the anti-defection law enacted, to which the 1984 NTR-Nadendla Bhaskara Rao crisis contributed?
x: The episode contributed to the anti-defection law enacted by the 52nd Constitutional Amendment, 1985.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the 2026 developments on the capital of Andhra Pradesh?
o: The AP Assembly passed a resolution on 28 March 2026.
The amendment made Hyderabad the sole capital of Andhra Pradesh.
The Lok Sabha passed the amendment Bill in June 2026.
The resolution sought naming Amaravati in Section 5(2) of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014.
x: The 2026 amendment made Amaravati, not Hyderabad, the sole capital of Andhra Pradesh.

s: Who is the Governor of Andhra Pradesh, with N. Chandrababu Naidu as Chief Minister and Amaravati as capital?
x: S. Abdul Nazeer is the Governor of Andhra Pradesh, whose capital is Amaravati and Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu.

s: Which of the following pairs (leader – national office) is correctly matched?
o: P.V. Narasimha Rao – Chairman, National Front
Neelam Sanjiva Reddy – Prime Minister of India
x: Damodaram Sanjivayya was AICC President. Sanjiva Reddy was President of India, P.V. Narasimha Rao Prime Minister and NTR Chairman of the National Front.

s: Who was the Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh during the Jai Andhra Movement of 1972?
x: P.V. Narasimha Rao was CM when the Supreme Court's Mulki verdict set off the Jai Andhra Movement.

s: In which year did the NTR government introduce the Mandal system of local administration in Andhra Pradesh?
x: NTR introduced the Mandal system from 1985; in 1983 he allowed a simple majority for no-confidence motions against Zilla Parishad vice-chairmen.

s: Who had the longest continuous tenure as Chief Minister of united Andhra Pradesh?
x: Chandrababu Naidu (1995–2004) had the longest continuous tenure.

s: In which year did Neelam Sanjiva Reddy become President of India?
x: He became President in 1977; in 1960 he was AICC President.

s: Which party did Nadendla Bhaskara Rao form in 1984?
x: Nadendla formed the Democratic Telugu Desam Party; Chenna Reddy formed the National Democratic Party.

s: Which state introduced Panchayat Raj on 2 October 1959, before Andhra Pradesh?
x: Rajasthan was first (2 Oct 1959); AP followed on 1 Nov 1959.

s: How many seats did the Congress win in the 1962 Andhra Pradesh Assembly election?
x: The Congress won 177 seats in 1962; the Communists won over 50.

s: Who was the last Chief Minister of united Andhra Pradesh?
x: N. Kiran Kumar Reddy (2010–14) was the last CM of united AP.

s: On which date did N.T. Rama Rao's Rs 2 per kg rice scheme begin?
x: The Rs 2/kg rice scheme began on 14 April 1983.

s: Who became Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh immediately after Damodaram Sanjivayya?
x: Sanjiva Reddy returned as CM (1962–64) after Sanjivayya.

s: After the Congress (I) was formed on 1 January 1978, who led the rival Reddy Congress?
x: Brahmananda Reddy led the Reddy Congress.

s: During which period did the Congress rule Andhra Pradesh uninterruptedly?
x: The Congress ruled without a break from 1956 to 1983.

s: Who served as Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh immediately before the imposition of President’s Rule in January 1973?
x: P.V. Narasimha Rao served as Chief Minister from 1971 until President’s Rule began on 18 January 1973.

s: Who had the shortest tenure as Chief Minister of united Andhra Pradesh, about 31 days in 1984?
x: Nadendla Bhaskara Rao served 31 days (16 Aug - 16 Sep 1984).

s: In which year did P.V. Narasimha Rao first become Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh?
x: The order was Sanjivayya (1960), Kasu Brahmananda Reddy (1964), P.V. Narasimha Rao (1971), T. Anjaiah (1980).

s: Who was the first Dalit Chief Minister in India?
x: Damodaram Sanjivayya, CM of AP from 11 January 1960, was the first Dalit CM in India.

s: Bhavanam Venkatarami Reddy was the first Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh to come from which House?
x: Bhavanam Venkatarami Reddy (Feb-Sep 1982) was the first CM of Andhra Pradesh from the Legislative Council.

s: E.V. Rama Reddy was the first holder of which anti-corruption post created by N.T. Rama Rao?
x: NTR created the Dharma Mahamatra post to fight corruption; its first holder was E.V. Rama Reddy.

s: In which year was the AP Land Reforms (Ceiling) Act passed by the P.V. Narasimha Rao ministry?
x: The AP Land Reforms (Ceiling) Act came in 1973 under the P.V. Narasimha Rao ministry.

s: On which date was Panchayat Raj introduced in Andhra Pradesh?
x: Andhra Pradesh introduced Panchayat Raj on 1 November 1959 under Neelam Sanjiva Reddy, after Rajasthan (2 October 1959).

s:
Arrange the following Chief Ministers of Andhra Pradesh in chronological order:
A. Jalagam Vengala Rao
B. N.T. Rama Rao
C. Marri Chenna Reddy
D. Neelam Sanjiva Reddy
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: Neelam Sanjiva Reddy (1956), Jalagam Vengala Rao (1973), Marri Chenna Reddy (1978), N.T. Rama Rao (1983).

s: Which of the following leaders never held the post of Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh?
x: Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao was the first Speaker, never CM; the others were Chief Ministers.

s: On which date did N.T. Rama Rao found the Telugu Desam Party?
x: NTR founded the TDP on 29 March 1982 and became CM on 9 January 1983.

s: In which year did Neelam Sanjiva Reddy leave the Chief Minister's post to join Lal Bahadur Shastri's cabinet as Union Minister?
x: In 1964 Neelam Sanjiva Reddy became Union Minister of Steel and Mines in Shastri's cabinet.

s: In which forest did Chief Minister Y.S. Rajasekhara Reddy die in a helicopter crash on 2 September 2009?
x: YSR died in a helicopter crash in the Nallamala forest on 2 September 2009.

s: Who succeeded Y.S. Rajasekhara Reddy as Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh in 2009?
x: After YSR's death in 2009, K. Rosaiah became Chief Minister.

s: Who was the Chief Minister of residual Andhra Pradesh from 2019 to 2024?
x: Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy was CM 2019-24; N. Chandrababu Naidu returned on 12 June 2024.

s: Who led the Swatantra Party in Andhra Pradesh in 1959?
x: In 1959 the Swatantra Party in AP was led by N.G. Ranga.

s: What is OCTOPUS, set up in Andhra Pradesh in 2007?
x: OCTOPUS (Organisation for Counter Terrorist Operations) is AP's anti-terror commando force, set up in 2007.

s: Which of the following pairs (force – role) is correctly matched?
x: Greyhounds is the anti-Naxal force; OCTOPUS is the anti-terror force.

s: Where did the N.T. Rama Rao government set up a Women's University?
x: Among NTR's reforms was the Women's University at Tirupati.

s: Which leader from Andhra Pradesh was the Chairman of the National Front?
x: N.T. Rama Rao was the Chairman of the National Front.

s: Who among the following was AICC President in 1960 and later Speaker of the Lok Sabha?
x: Neelam Sanjiva Reddy was AICC President (1960), later Lok Sabha Speaker and President of India (1977).

s: Who is the Deputy Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh in 2026?
x: In 2026 the CM is N. Chandrababu Naidu and the Deputy CM is K. Pawan Kalyan.

s: Which party did Marri Chenna Reddy form in 1984?
x: In 1984 Chenna Reddy formed the National Democratic Party; Nadendla formed the Democratic Telugu Desam Party.

s: On which date did N.T. Rama Rao found the Telugu Desam Party?
x: NTR founded the TDP on 29 March 1982, not 29 May.

s: Which award settled the Andhra-Madras boundary and gave Tiruttani to Tamil Nadu?
x: The Pataskar Award settled the boundary; the Wanchoo Committee (7 Feb 1953) was headed by K.N. Wanchoo, CJ of Rajasthan HC.

s: On which issue did Tanguturi Prakasam's ministry in Andhra State lose its majority?
x: Tanguturi Prakasam's ministry lost its majority over the prohibition issue, leading to mid-term polls in 1955.

s: Why was the Wanchoo Committee (1953) appointed?
o: Recommend the reorganisation of all Indian states on linguistic lines
Identify the financial and administrative problems of forming Andhra State
Settle the boundary dispute between Andhra and Madras
Frame safeguards for Telangana before the merger
x: The Wanchoo Committee, appointed in December 1952 after Potti Sriramulu's death, was asked to identify the financial and administrative problems of forming Andhra State (APPSC G2 2012); it reported on 7 February 1953. Linguistic reorganisation of all states was the SRC's task, the Andhra-Madras border was settled by the Pataskar Award, and Telangana safeguards came from the 1956 Gentlemen's Agreement.

s: Who became Chief Minister of Andhra State after the 1955 mid-term polls?
x: Bezawada Gopala Reddy became CM in 1955; he was the last CM of Andhra State.

s: Neelam Sanjiva Reddy served as Deputy Chief Minister of which state before becoming the first Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh?
x: In Andhra State (1953) Prakasam was CM and N. Sanjiva Reddy was Deputy CM.

s: The 1957 Assembly elections in Andhra Pradesh were held only in Telangana, covering how many seats?
x: The 1957 elections were held only in Telangana and covered 79 seats.

s: In 1956, the 11 districts of Andhra State were merged with how many Telugu-speaking districts of Hyderabad State?
x: The 11 Andhra districts merged with nine Telugu-speaking districts of Hyderabad State.

s: Where did the Andhra Legislature meet to resolve unanimously in favour of the merger before the formation of Andhra Pradesh?
x: The Andhra Legislature unanimously backed the merger at Kurnool, and both ministries resigned.

s: Which city became the capital of Andhra Pradesh in 1956, replacing Kurnool?
x: Hyderabad became the capital of Andhra Pradesh in 1956, replacing Kurnool, which had served as the capital of Andhra State from 1953 to 1956.

s: Which name did the draft Bill propose for the state formed on 1 November 1956?
x: The draft Bill used 'Andhra Telangana'; the Seventh Amendment Bill in the Lok Sabha settled on 'Andhra Pradesh'.

s: Andhra Pradesh was formed on 1 November 1956 under which law and on what basis?
o: Government of India Act, 1935; religious composition
Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014; economic viability
x: AP was formed under the States Reorganisation Act, 1956, on the basis of linguistic reorganisation (APPSC GS 2023), merging Andhra State with the Telugu districts of Hyderabad State. The Andhra State Act created Andhra State in 1953; the 1935 Act and APRA 2014 belong to other events.

s: Who was the first Leader of the Opposition in the newly formed Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly?
x: Puchalapalli Sundarayya was the first Leader of the Opposition in the newly formed Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly.

s: On which date did the separate High Court of Andhra Pradesh begin functioning at Amaravati?
x: After the common High Court (2014-2018), AP's separate High Court began at Amaravati on 1 January 2019.

s: Who was the first Deputy Speaker of the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly?
x: Kalluri Subbarao was the first Deputy Speaker; Kaleswara Rao was the first Speaker.

s: The Andhra Pradesh Legislative Council, constituted in 1958, had how many members?
x: The Council was constituted in 1958 with 90 members.

s: From which date did the High Court at Hyderabad for Andhra Pradesh begin functioning?
x: The High Court functioned at Hyderabad from 5 November 1956.

s: After serving as the first Governor of Kerala, Burgula Ramakrishna Rao became Governor of which state?
x: Burgula became first Governor of Kerala (1956), then of Uttar Pradesh.

s: Which name did the Communists propose for the new state in 1956?
x: The draft Bill proposed 'Andhra Telangana', the Communists 'Visalandhra'; the final name was 'Andhra Pradesh'.

s: Which of the following was a reason for choosing Hyderabad as the capital of Andhra Pradesh?
o: The SRC's view and the Mahasabha demand
The Kurnool Assembly vote of 80 to 79
x: Hyderabad was chosen on the SRC's view and the Visalandhra Mahasabha's demand.

s: With 40 members from Hyderabad and 119 from Andhra, what was the Congress strength in the new AP Assembly?
x: 40 + 119 = 159 Congress members.

s: Which post did Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao hold in the newly formed Andhra Pradesh in 1956?
o: First Speaker of the Legislative Assembly
First Chairman of the Legislative Council
x: Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao was the first Speaker; Sundarayya was first Leader of the Opposition and Madapati Hanumantha Rao first Council Chairman.

s: On which date did Jawaharlal Nehru inaugurate the state of Andhra Pradesh?
x: Andhra Pradesh was formed and inaugurated by Nehru on 1 November 1956.

s: Who was the first Governor of Andhra Pradesh?
x: C.M. Trivedi, already Governor of Andhra State, became the first Governor of Andhra Pradesh in 1956.

s: Which body changed the name 'Andhra Telangana' in the draft Bill to 'Andhra Pradesh'?
x: The draft Bill said 'Andhra Telangana'; the Joint Select Committee changed it to 'Andhra Pradesh'.

s: Which portfolio did Bezawada Gopala Reddy hold in the first ministry of Andhra Pradesh (1956)?
x: Bezawada Gopala Reddy was Finance Minister; Kasu Brahmananda Reddy had Local Bodies and J.V. Narsing Rao Irrigation and Electricity.

s: Which Chief Minister abolished the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Council in 1985?
x: The Council set up on 1 July 1958 was abolished in 1985 under N.T. Rama Rao.

s: In which year was the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Council revived?
x: The Council was revived in 2007 under Y.S. Rajasekhara Reddy.

s: The grievance arising from the alleged violations of the Gentlemen's Agreement contributed to which movement?
x: The alleged violations, especially concerning employment, domicile and revenue surplus, contributed to the Jai Telangana agitation of 1969.

s: Which Article of the Constitution reflects the legacy of the Gentlemen's Agreement's domicile-related protection?
x: Article 371D and local-cadre arrangements reflect the Agreement's domicile protection.

s: To which State(s) did Section 97 of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 extend Article 371D?
o: The State of Andhra Pradesh or the State of Telangana
Only the State of Andhra Pradesh
x: Section 97 extended the operation of Article 371D to the State of Andhra Pradesh or the State of Telangana.

s: Who was the Chief Minister of Hyderabad State at the time of the Gentlemen's Agreement?
x: Burgula was CM of Hyderabad State, K.V. Ranga Reddy its Deputy CM, and Bezawada Gopala Reddy CM of Andhra State.

s: The Gentlemen's Agreement of 1956 adapted the model of which earlier pact for settling regional apprehensions?
x: Like the Sribagh Pact, the Gentlemen's Agreement addressed regional fears through a moral and political understanding rather than a constitutional settlement.

s: The Gentlemen's Agreement was signed at which of the following places?
x: The agreement was signed at Hyderabad House in New Delhi. Some accounts refer to the venue as Hyderabad Guest House, Delhi, but the commonly recorded venue is Hyderabad House.

s: Under the Gentlemen's Agreement, what minimum share of seats in technical institutions was assured to Telangana students?
x: The agreement gave Telangana students admission priority or at least one-third of the seats in technical institutions, whichever was more favourable.

s: The domicile safeguard associated with recruitment in Telangana required residence for how many years?
x: The agreed safeguard referred to Mulki or domicile rules requiring 12 years of residence for recruitment in Telangana.

s: After how many years was the financial arrangement for Telangana under the Gentlemen's Agreement to be reviewed?
x: Common costs were shared proportionately, Telangana's surplus was to be spent in Telangana, and the arrangement reviewed after five years.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Services — Proportionate retrenchment and recruitment according to population ratio under domicile rules
Land — Exclusive power of the Union Government over agricultural sales
Urdu — Abolition from Telangana administration immediately after the agreement
Prohibition — Uniform compulsory prohibition throughout Andhra Pradesh
x: The services safeguard provided for recruitment according to population ratio under domicile rules and proportionate retrenchment from both regions. The other pairs contradict the agreed provisions.

s: For how long was Urdu to be kept in Telangana's administration and courts under the Gentlemen's Agreement (1956)?
x: Under the Gentlemen's Agreement, Urdu was to be kept in Telangana's administration and courts for five years, and then reviewed.

s: Under the Gentlemen's Agreement, at least how many of the portfolios of Home, Finance, Revenue, Planning and Development, and Commerce and Industry were to go to Telangana?
x: At least two of these five portfolios were to go to Telangana.

s: After how many years was the working of the Telangana Regional Committee to be reviewed?
x: The Committee's working was to be reviewed after ten years; disputes with the State Government went to the Centre.

s: How was Telangana's revenue surplus to be used under the Gentlemen's Agreement?
o: Used to build the new capital
x: The promise was that Telangana's surplus would be spent only on Telangana.

s: In what capacity did Gouthu Latchanna sign the Gentlemen's Agreement?
x: Gouthu Latchanna signed as a Minister from Andhra.

s: Who signed the Gentlemen's Agreement as President of the Hyderabad PCC?
x: J.V. Narsing Rao signed as Hyderabad PCC President; Alluri Satyanarayana Raju was APCC President.

s: Under the Gentlemen's Agreement, which body was to control the sale of agricultural land in Telangana?
x: Sale of agricultural land was to be controlled by the Regional Council.

s: Under the Gentlemen's Agreement, from which regions were the Chief Minister and Deputy Chief Minister to be chosen?
x: The CM and Deputy CM were to come from different regions.

s: Which of the following was NOT a provision of the Gentlemen's Agreement?
o: Prohibition in Telangana left to Telangana legislators
Cabinet seats shared 3:1 between Andhra and Telangana
Recruitment to services by population ratio
x: The cabinet ratio was 60:40, not 3:1.

s: Who among the following was NOT a signatory to the Gentlemen's Agreement of 1956?
x: The eight signatories included Gouthu Latchanna, Alluri Satyanarayana Raju and K.V. Ranga Reddy; Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao did not sign.

s: Who signed the Gentlemen's Agreement as Deputy Chief Minister of Hyderabad State?
x: K.V. Ranga Reddy signed as Deputy CM of Hyderabad; Neelam Sanjiva Reddy signed as Deputy CM of Andhra State.

s: How many leaders from Telangana signed the Gentlemen's Agreement of 20 February 1956?
x: The Agreement had eight signatories: four from Andhra and four from Telangana.

s: In what ratio was cabinet representation to be shared between Andhra and Telangana under the Gentlemen's Agreement?
x: The Agreement fixed cabinet shares at 60:40 (Andhra:Telangana), not 3:1.

s: Which agreement was signed at Hyderabad House, New Delhi, on 20 February 1956?
x: The Gentlemen's Agreement between Andhra and Telangana leaders was signed at Hyderabad House, New Delhi, on 20 February 1956.

s: In what capacity did Alluri Satyanarayana Raju sign the Gentlemen's Agreement?
o: Deputy Chief Minister of Andhra State
x: Alluri Satyanarayana Raju signed as APCC President, one of the four Andhra signatories.

s:
Match the following signatories of the Gentlemen's Agreement with the posts they held:
List-I (Signatory)
a. Neelam Sanjiva Reddy
b. Marri Chenna Reddy
c. Alluri Satyanarayana Raju
d. Burgula Ramakrishna Rao
List-II (Post)
1. CM, Hyderabad
2. APCC President
3. Minister, Hyderabad

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: Sanjiva Reddy was Deputy CM of Andhra, Chenna Reddy a Hyderabad minister, Alluri the APCC President and Burgula the CM of Hyderabad.

s: Under the Gentlemen's Agreement, at least how many Muslim ministers were to be from Telangana?
x: The cabinet was to be shared 60:40 with at least one Muslim minister from Telangana.

s: Through which provision was the Telangana Regional Committee under the Gentlemen's Agreement given constitutional backing?
o: Article 371(1) and the 1958 Regional Committee Order
A separate Schedule of the Constitution
x: Backing came from Article 371(1) (Seventh Amendment, 1956) and the AP Regional Committee Order, 1958.

s: For how long was the Telangana Regional Committee extended in 1968?
x: It was extended for five years in 1968 and wound up after the 32nd Amendment (1973).

s: What did the Presidential Order of 1975 relating to Andhra Pradesh mainly deal with?
o: Transfer of the Andhra High Court to Amaravati
Creation of a separate Legislative Council for Telangana
Organisation of local cadres and regulation of direct recruitment
Division of the Krishna and Godavari rivers
x: The 1975 Presidential Order was the AP Public Employment (Organisation of Local Cadres and Regulation of Direct Recruitment) Order.

s: Article 371D of the Constitution, relating to Andhra Pradesh, was inserted by which Constitutional Amendment?
x: Article 371D was inserted by the 32nd Amendment, 1973, implementing the Six-Point Formula. The 33rd is a common wrong answer (some sources print it); the 31st and 42nd Amendments dealt with other matters.

s: After which event was the Telangana Regional Committee wound up?
x: It was extended five years in 1968 and wound up after the 32nd Amendment, 1973.

s: Which of the following about the Telangana Regional Committee is NOT correct?
o: The Chief Minister was an ex officio member
Its members included Telangana MLAs and MPs elected by Telangana legislators
Telangana ministers were ex officio members
Its powers covered irrigation, education and recruitment
x: Telangana ministers except the CM were ex officio members.

s: Who was the first Chairman of the Telangana Regional Committee?
x: K. Achyuta Reddy, Congress MLA from Kodangal, was elected the first Chairman of the Telangana Regional Committee (1958).

s: K. Achyuta Reddy, the first Chairman of the Telangana Regional Committee, was an MLA from which constituency?
x: K. Achyuta Reddy was the Congress MLA from Kodangal.

s: Who, along with Jonnavittula Gurunatham, sketched the idea of a united Andhra in 1912?
x: Unnava Lakshminarayana and Jonnavittula Gurunatham sketched it in 1912; Nyapati Subbarao proposed one rule for all Telugu areas in 1914.

s: Who coined the expression ‘Visalandhra’ and wrote Visalandhralo Prajarajyam?
x: Puchalapalli Sundarayya coined the expression ‘Visalandhra’ and authored Visalandhralo Prajarajyam.

s: What did the term 'Visalandhra', meaning 'Greater Andhra', refer to?
o: A separate Telangana state under Hyderabad
One state for all Telugu-speaking people of the Madras and Hyderabad regions
A federation of all southern Indian states
The merger of Andhra with the Madras Presidency without Hyderabad
x: Visalandhra, or Greater Andhra, envisaged one state for Telugu-speaking people living in the Madras region and Nizam’s Hyderabad.

s: In which year did Swami Sitaram undertake his fast for the Andhra cause?
x: Swami Sitaram's fast came in 1951, after the Dhar Commission (1948) and the Visalandhra Mahasabha (1949), and before Andhra State (1953).

s: Who proposed one rule for all Telugu areas at the second Andhra Mahasabha in 1914?
x: Nyapati Subbarao made the proposal at the 1914 Mahasabha.

s: In 1954, who said the Visalandhra idea was 50 years old, as old as the Andhra Movement?
x: Madapati Hanumantha Rao said so in 1954.

s: In which year did the Andhra Congress Swaraj Party manifesto, a root of the Visalandhra idea, come out?
x: The Swaraj Party manifesto came in 1936.

s:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
1. Visalandhra Mahasabha
2. Dhar Commission
3. Swami Sitaram's fast
4. States Reorganisation Commission
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: Dhar Commission (1948), Visalandhra Mahasabha (1949), Swami Sitaram's fast (1951), SRC (1953).

s: The first Visalandhra Mahasabha at Warangal demanded that Hyderabad State be divided into three linguistic parts. Which city did it want as the capital?
x: The first Mahasabha called for Hyderabad as the capital and for Hyderabad State to be divided into three linguistic parts.

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
x: The Socialists' joint Andhra-Hyderabad meeting was at Kurnool on 21-22 March 1954. 13-14 June 1954, Hyderabad was the second Mahasabha (not the APCC, which met at Kurnool on 30 Sep 1953); 12-13 Feb 1950, Warangal was the first Mahasabha session, not the second; 26 Nov 1949, Vijayawada was the founding of the Visalandhra Mahasabha rather than its first session.

s: Who presided over the 1950 session of the Visalandhra Mahasabha?
x: Hayagreevachari presided over the 1950 session of the Visalandhra Mahasabha.

s: In which year was the second Visalandhra Mahasabha held at Hyderabad?
x: The second Mahasabha met at Hyderabad in June 1954, after the founding (1949), the Warangal session (1950) and the APCC Kurnool resolution (1953).

s: Which city did the APCC meeting at Kurnool on 30 September 1953 want as the capital of Visalandhra?
x: The 1953 Kurnool meeting, associated with Neelam Sanjiva Reddy, demanded Visalandhra with Hyderabad as capital.

s: In which year did Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao found the Visalandhra Mahasabha at Vijayawada?
x: He founded it on 26 November 1949 and raised the demand at the 1951 Bangalore Congress manifesto meeting.

s: Who presided over the second Visalandhra Mahasabha at Hyderabad in June 1954?
x: Sri Sri presided in 1954; Hayagreevachari presided over the 1950 Warangal session.

s: In June 1953, the Hyderabad Congress proposed splitting Hyderabad State into Visalandhra, United Maharashtra and which other unit?
x: The three-way split was Visalandhra, United Maharashtra and United Karnataka; it was rejected in 1954.

s: The APCC resolution of January 1950 proposed Hyderabad as the permanent capital. Which city did it propose as the temporary capital?
x: The January 1950 APCC resolution: Madras temporary, Hyderabad permanent capital.

s: Where was the 1951 Congress manifesto meeting held at which Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao raised Visalandhra?
x: He raised it at Bangalore in 1951 and resigned when no decision came.

s: Where was the Visalandhra Mahasabha founded on 26 November 1949?
x: Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao founded the Visalandhra Mahasabha at Vijayawada in 1949; its first session was at Warangal in 1950.
