3. Hyderabad
4. Warangal
x: The Mahasabha was founded at Vijayawada (1949), met first at Warangal (1950) and then at Hyderabad (1954); the APCC met at Kurnool on 30 September 1953.

s: Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao translated whose speech into Telugu at Vijayawada?
x: Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao translated Gandhi's Vijayawada speech into Telugu.

s: Who wrote 'The Emergence of Andhra Pradesh'?
x: K.V. Narayana Rao wrote the book; Devulapalli Ramanuja Rao contributed pamphlets for Visalandhra.

s: Who started the Visalandhra paper and became the first General Secretary of the CPI(M) in 1964?
x: P. Sundarayya started the Visalandhra paper and became the CPI(M)'s first General Secretary in 1964.

s: The Congress was initially cold towards the Visalandhra proposal because the idea came from which party?
x: The idea came from the Communists, and the Congress feared a united state might give them a majority.

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Mahila Sabha — Supported Visalandhra at Hyderabad in May 1954
Praja Socialist Party under Mahadeva Singh — Opposed Visalandhra
People’s Democratic Front — Congress electoral front in Hyderabad State in 1952
Hindu Mahasabha — Supported Visalandhra at Hyderabad in May 1954
x: The People’s Democratic Front was the Communists’ electoral front in Hyderabad State in 1952, not the Congress front. The other pairs are correctly matched.

s: From which place was the magazine 'Nilgiri', associated with the press of the Visalandhra period in Telangana, published?
x: Nilgiri was published from Nalgonda (APPSC G2 2012). Vijayawada was the headquarters of the Andhra Communist Party; Warangal hosted the 1950 Mahasabha session; Hyderabad hosted the 1954 session, not this magazine.

s: Who wrote 'Enni Naalla Swapnamidi'?
x: Dasarathi wrote 'Enni Naalla Swapnamidi', while Kaloji wrote 'Emaanandam ... Eenadu'.

s: Where was the headquarters of the Andhra Communist Party, of which the Hyderabad State Communist Party was practically a branch?
x: It worked as a branch of the Andhra party at Vijayawada; the Communists propagated Visalandhra.

s: Of which party was the People's Democratic Front (1952) in Hyderabad State the electoral front?
x: The PDF was the Communists' electoral front in 1952, not the Congress's.

s: With whom was the paper 'Imroz' associated?
x: Imroz was Shoebullah Khan's; Rayyat was Mandumula Narsing Rao's.

s: When was the Communist daily 'Visalandhra' started?
x: The Visalandhra daily began in June 1952 at Sundarayya's initiative.

s: Who among the following was NOT a Communist leader of the Visalandhra campaign in Telangana?
x: Marri Chenna Reddy opposed Visalandhra throughout; the others were Communist leaders.

s: Who wrote 'Emaanandam ... Eenadu'?
x: Kaloji wrote it; Dasarathi wrote 'Enni Naalla Swapnamidi'.

s: Who wrote pamphlets for the Visalandhra campaign?
x: Pamphlets for Visalandhra were written by Devulapalli Ramanuja Rao, and also Kodati Rajalingam, Hayagrivachari and Paga Pulla Reddy.

s: Regarding the Hyderabad Congress, which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: June 1953 – Hyderabad PCC delegation met the SRC
1954 – Telangana convention backed a separate Telangana
November 1955 – Resolution for dividing Hyderabad State into three parts
8 July 1954 – Hyderabad PCC delegation met the SRC
x: The Hyderabad PCC delegation met the SRC on 8 July 1954. The three-part resolution was of June 1953 and was rejected in 1954; separate Telangana was backed in November 1955.

s: What did a Hyderabad PCC delegation ask the SRC for on 8 July 1954?
o: A self-sufficient Telangana of 9 districts with Bastar and parts of Chanda
x: The delegation (Heda, J.V. Narsing Rao, Arige Ramaswamy) sought a self-sufficient Telangana.

s: Who backed a separate Telangana at the Telangana convention of November 1955?
x: Harishchandra Heda backed separate Telangana at the November 1955 convention.

s: Which party in Hyderabad, under Mahadev Singh, opposed Visalandhra and wanted a separate Telangana?
x: The Hyderabad PSP under Mahadev Singh stood for a separate Telangana.

s: Who described the Visalandhra movement as “Andhra imperialism” in October 1953?
x: Jawaharlal Nehru referred to the Visalandhra movement as “Andhra imperialism” in October 1953.

s: In the 1954 Visalandhra discussions, who warned that a separate Telangana would be weak and vulnerable to suppression of democratic forces?
x: Swami Ramananda Tirtha strongly supported Visalandhra and gave this warning.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Sri Sri — President of the Second Visalandhra Mahasabha
Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao — Founder of Visalandhra Mahasabha
Marri Chenna Reddy — Strong supporter of Visalandhra throughout
x: Marri Chenna Reddy was an opponent of Visalandhra. The other three pairs are correctly matched.

s: Which cause did Swami Ramananda Tirtha, Burgula Ramakrishna Rao, Mandumula Narsing Rao and Pandit Narendraji all support?
x: All four supported the Visalandhra movement.

s: Who preferred retaining Hyderabad as a multilingual state in 1949?
x: C. Rajagopalachari preferred retaining Hyderabad as a multilingual state in 1949.

s: With whom is the statement 'Visalandhra nirmanam... is the mother's right of all Andhras' associated?
x: Tanguturi Prakasam used this expression while supporting the construction of Visalandhra.

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: K.V. Ranga Reddy — Initially supported Visalandhra, later supported separate Telangana
x: Tanguturi Prakasam supported Visalandhra. Marri Chenna Reddy and Mahadeva Singh opposed the merger, while K.V. Ranga Reddy changed his position from support to separate Telangana.

s: Which leader backed Visalandhra but turned against it after becoming Telangana Congress president?
x: K.V. Ranga Reddy changed sides; Marri Chenna Reddy opposed throughout.

s: Which leader opposed Visalandhra throughout?
x: Marri Chenna Reddy was against throughout; Ranga Reddy and Kaloji changed their stands.

s:
Consider the following statements about leaders in the Visalandhra debate:
1. Kaloji supported Visalandhra and later opposed it.
2. Marri Chenna Reddy changed sides after becoming Telangana Congress president.
3. Makhdoom Mohiuddin was among the educated Muslims who supported it.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 2 is wrong: it was K.V. Ranga Reddy who changed sides; Chenna Reddy opposed throughout.

s: In 1955, Burgula Ramakrishna Rao, who had earlier backed a separate Telangana, came to support which course?
o: Early merger of Telangana with Andhra
x: Burgula Ramakrishna Rao moved from a separate Telangana to an early merger with Andhra in 1955.

s: Which one of the following was NOT an argument advanced in favour of Visalandhra?
o: Combination of Andhra agriculture and coastline with Telangana minerals and industry
Integrated planning of the Krishna and Godavari basins
Permanent protection of separate Telangana political institutions
x: Protection of separate Telangana political institutions was not a pro-Visalandhra argument. The other three were arguments advanced in favour of unification.

s: The argument that Telangana could exist as a separate State rested on which of its advantages over Andhra State?
x: Telangana's higher per capita income and revenue than Andhra State made it economically viable on its own.

s: Before the 1956 merger, which rules did Telangana fear might be weakened, hurting local employment?
x: The employment concern was weakening of the Mulki Rules; other fears concerned the revenue surplus and regional disparities.

s: According to the Communists' agrarian argument for Visalandhra, what would unification help to do?
o: Transfer all land revenue to Hyderabad
Push land reforms and weaken feudal structures
x: The Communist agrarian argument held that unification could promote land reform and weaken feudal structures.

s: Which of the following was a Telangana apprehension about the merger?
o: Telangana's revenue surplus being spent elsewhere
x: Diversion of the revenue surplus was a Telangana fear; the others were arguments for Visalandhra.

s: Integrated planning of which rivers formed the river-waters argument for Visalandhra?
x: Integrated Krishna–Godavari planning was the river-waters argument.

s: Under paragraph 386 of the SRC report, by what majority did Telangana's legislature have to approve merger with Andhra after the 1961 elections?
x: The SRC recommended a separate Telangana initially, with merger after the 1961 elections only on a two-thirds majority of the Telangana legislature.

s: Who among the following was NOT a member of the States Reorganisation Commission?
x: Fazl Ali, H.N. Kunzru and K.M. Panikkar were the members of the States Reorganisation Commission. Harishchandra Heda was associated with Telangana political resolutions, not with the Commission.

s: In which year did the Andhra Assembly unanimously pass Bezawada Gopala Reddy's resolution on merger?
x: The resolution, giving Telangana priority and population-based shares, was passed in 1955.

s: In the Hyderabad Assembly vote on Visalandhra, how many members voted against?
x: The vote was 103 for, 29 against and 15 neutral.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Nehru announced the SRC in the Lok Sabha – 29 December 1953
Report of the States Reorganisation Commission – 1955
x: The SRC report came in 1955. Nehru announced the Commission on 22 December 1953, it was constituted on 29 December 1953, and the Mahasabha was founded in 1949.

s: Which of the following territorial changes was recommended in relation to Hyderabad State by the States Reorganisation Commission?
o: Raichur and Gulbarga to Andhra, and Marathwada to Mysore
Marathwada to Andhra, and the Kannada areas to Telangana
Raichur and Gulbarga to Mysore, and Marathwada to be detached
x: The Commission recommended that Raichur and Gulbarga go to Mysore and that Marathwada be detached from Hyderabad State.

s: The Nizam Andhra Mahasabha developed out of which organisation founded in 1921?
x: The Nizam Andhra Mahasabha grew out of the Andhra Jana Sangham, which was founded in 1921.

s: In which year did the Mulki rules of Hyderabad State originate?
x: The Mulki rules date from 1888 and were tightened by the Nizam's farman of 1919.

s: Under whose ministry did the Mulki agitation of 1952 take place?
x: It occurred under the Burgula ministry; police firing near City College, Hyderabad, killed students.

s: On which date was the Join Indian Union Movement launched in Hyderabad?
x: It began on 7 August 1947 against the Nizam's plan to keep Hyderabad independent; 17 September 1948 is the date of integration after Operation Polo.

s: Where did police firing kill students during the 1952 Mulki agitation?
x: The firing of 3–4 September 1952 was near City College, Hyderabad.

s: Who headed the inquiry commission into the 1952 City College firing?
x: Justice Pingali Jaganmohan Reddy reported on 28 December 1952.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Mulki rules of Hyderabad State:
1. They were made stricter by the Nizam's farman of 1919.
2. Only residents of about 15 years got local jobs.
3. The 1952 inquiry led to a major change in the Mulki rules.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 3 is wrong: no major change in the Mulki rules followed the 1952 inquiry.

s: Who was the Speaker of the Hyderabad Assembly at the time of the merger?
x: Kashinatha Rao was the Speaker at the merger.

s: Through which operation was Hyderabad State integrated with India on 17 September 1948?
x: Hyderabad was integrated through Operation Polo.

s:
Assertion (A): Swamy Ramananda Tirtha was a key personality of the Join Indian Union Movement.
Reason (R): The Join Indian Union Movement opposed the Nizam’s declaration of Hyderabad as an independent sovereign state.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true but R does not explain A: Ramananda Tirtha led the movement, and its aim was to oppose the Nizam's independence. The aim does not explain why he was its leader.

s: Which agitation of 1883 marked the beginning of public political consciousness in Hyderabad State?
x: The Chanda Railway Scheme agitation of 1883 is seen as the start of public political consciousness in Hyderabad State.

s: Swami Ramananda Tirtha, leader of the Join Indian Union Movement, founded which organisation?
x: Swami Ramananda Tirtha founded the Hyderabad State Congress and led the Join Indian Union Movement from 7 August 1947.

s: The first Andhra Mahasabha in the Nizam's Hyderabad State was held at which place in 1930, and who presided over it?
x: The first Andhra Mahasabha met at Jogipet in 1930 under Suravaram Pratapa Reddy. Warangal and Hayagreevachari belong to the 1950 Visalandhra Mahasabha session; Vijayawada and Kaleswara Rao to the founding of the Visalandhra Mahasabha (1949); Burgula did not preside at Jogipet.

s:
Consider the following statements about Swami Ramananda Tirtha:
1. He founded the Hyderabad State Congress.
2. He opposed Visalandhra at the second Visalandhra Mahasabha of 1954.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Swami Ramananda Tirtha founded the Hyderabad State Congress and strongly backed Visalandhra at the 1954 Hyderabad Mahasabha, so statement 2 is wrong.

s: Hyderabad State was classified as a Part B State during which of the following periods?
x: Hyderabad State was a Part B State from 1950 until 31 October 1956, immediately before the formation of Andhra Pradesh.

s: Which one of the following pairs relating to the pre-merger states is NOT correctly matched?
o: Andhra State — Bezawada Gopala Reddy as Chief Minister at the time of merger
Andhra State — Laxmi Narasimham as Speaker at the time of merger
Hyderabad State — Burgula Ramakrishna Rao as Chief Minister at the time of merger
Hyderabad State — Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao as Speaker at the time of merger
x: The pair in option d is incorrect. Kashinatha Rao was the Speaker of Hyderabad State at the time of merger; Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao became the first Speaker of Andhra Pradesh.

s: As which entry number in the First Schedule was Telangana added by Section 10 of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014?
x: Section 10 added Telangana as entry 29; the Act was made under Articles 3 and 4, needing no Article 368 amendment.

s: A major criticism of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 is that it was passed without whose consent?
x: The Act was passed without the consent of the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly.

s: Which Article of the Constitution was amended in relation to the Legislative Council of Telangana?
x: Article 168 was changed in relation to the Legislative Council of Telangana. Article 371D was extended to Telangana separately.

s: For how many years were existing admission quotas under Article 371D continued under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014?
x: The Act continued the existing Article 371D admission quotas for ten years and extended Article 371D to Telangana.

s: Which Part of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 deals with the High Court?
x: Part IV deals with the High Court; Parts III, VI and VIII cover legislatures, assets and liabilities, and services.

s: How many Parts, Sections and Schedules does the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 consist of?
x: The Act has 12 Parts, 108 Sections (Section 108 is the removal-of-difficulties clause) and 13 Schedules (the Thirteenth lists the institutions and infrastructure promised to AP). The other combinations alter one or more of these numbers.

s: Which Section of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 extended Article 371D to Telangana?
x: Section 97 extended Article 371D to Telangana; Section 10 added Telangana as Entry 29 in the First Schedule.

s: The Apex Council and the Krishna and Godavari River Management Boards are provided for under which sections of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014?
x: Sections 84 and 85 provide for the Apex Council and the Krishna and Godavari River Management Boards respectively.

s: Which Section of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 made Hyderabad the common capital?
x: Section 5 dealt with Hyderabad as common capital; Section 3 formed Telangana, Section 6 the capital expert committee and Section 8 the Governor's security role.

s: Regarding the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, which pair is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Sections 84–85 – Polavaram as a national project
Section 46 – Finance Commission award, grants and backward-area package
Section 90 – Polavaram as a national project
x: Sections 84–85 provide for the Apex Council and the River Management Boards; Polavaram is under Section 90.

s: Under Section 5 of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, for what maximum period was Hyderabad to be the common capital?
x: Section 5 made Hyderabad the common capital for not more than ten years.

s: Which Part of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 deals with the formation of Telangana, the common capital and the common Governor?
x: Part II (Sections 3-11) covers the reorganisation itself; Part I is preliminary, Part VI deals with assets and liabilities and Part XII with legal and miscellaneous provisions.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Section 90 — Polavaram declared a national project
Section 50 — Recovery of tax arrears by place of assessment
Section 56 — Tax refunds by population ratio
Section 94 — Extension of Article 371D to Telangana
x: Section 94 deals with fiscal support, including tax incentives, a special development package for backward areas and Central support for the new capital. Article 371D was extended to Telangana under Section 97.

s: Which Section of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 provided an expert committee for Andhra Pradesh's new capital?
x: Section 6 provided the expert committee; Section 5 made Hyderabad the common capital.

s: Under which Section of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 was Polavaram declared a national project?
x: Section 90 deals with the Polavaram national project.

s: Under Section 26 of the AP Reorganisation Act, to how many seats was Andhra Pradesh's Assembly to rise from 175?
x: Delimitation was to raise AP from 175 to 225 and Telangana from 119 to 153.

s: What does Section 46 of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 deal with?
o: Splitting the Finance Commission award and a backward-area package
x: Section 46 covers the Finance Commission award split and the backward-area package.

s: On what basis are tax arrears apportioned under Section 50 of the AP Reorganisation Act?
x: Section 50: arrears by place of assessment; Section 56: refunds by population.

s: Where did the common High Court sit under Sections 30-31 of the AP Reorganisation Act?
x: The common High Court sat at Hyderabad until AP got its own High Court.

s: Which Part of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 contains the provisions amending Articles 168 and 371D of the Constitution?
x: Part XII contains legal and miscellaneous provisions and amends Articles 168 and 371D.

s: Under Section 8 of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, for what was the Governor given special responsibility in the common capital?
o: Security of life, liberty and property of its residents
Allocation of Krishna and Godavari waters
x: Section 8 made the Governor specially responsible for the security of residents of the common capital Hyderabad.

s: Under Section 3 of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, the new State of Telangana was formed with how many districts?
x: Section 3 formed Telangana with 10 districts; residuary Andhra Pradesh kept 13.

s: Under Section 26 of the AP Reorganisation Act, to how many seats was the Telangana Assembly to rise from 119?
x: Section 26 provides for AP 175 to 225 and Telangana 119 to 153, subject to Article 170.

s: On which date did Telangana come into existence as the 29th State of India?
x: Telangana was formed on 2 June 2014 under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, as the 29th State. The other dates are distractors: 1 November is the old AP formation day and 2 October is Gandhi Jayanti.

s: Which of the following about the apportionment ratio under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 is NOT correct?
o: The larger share went to Andhra Pradesh
The ratio was based on the 2011 Census population
Assets and liabilities were split equally, 50 : 50
x: The broad population ratio was 58.32:41.68 (AP:Telangana), from the 2011 Census, not an equal 50:50 split.

s: How many Assembly seats were initially allocated to Telangana under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014?
x: Telangana got 119 seats and Andhra Pradesh 175; 225 and 153 are the proposed future increases under Section 26.

s: On which date did the Rajya Sabha pass the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Bill?
x: Lok Sabha 18 Feb, Rajya Sabha 20 Feb 2014.

s: On which date did the Lok Sabha pass the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Bill?
x: The Lok Sabha passed it on 18 February 2014 and the Rajya Sabha on 20 February 2014.

s: Under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, which pair is correctly matched?
o: Eleventh Schedule – Coal, oil, gas and power
Twelfth Schedule – Public sector undertakings and corporations
x: The Tenth Schedule covers State institutions; the Ninth covers PSUs, the Eleventh irrigation projects and the Twelfth coal, oil, gas and power.

s: Which one of the following was a consequence faced by the residuary State of Andhra Pradesh after reorganisation?
o: It lost Hyderabad and faced revenue deficits.
It became responsible for the entire Telangana public debt.
It acquired all districts of the former State of Hyderabad.
It retained Hyderabad and obtained a revenue surplus.
x: The residuary State of Andhra Pradesh lost Hyderabad, a major revenue-generating centre, and faced revenue deficits after bifurcation.

s: Provisions for IIT, NIT, IIM, AIIMS and a new railway zone for Andhra Pradesh are in which Schedule of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014?
x: The Thirteenth Schedule lists these institutions, central and tribal universities and infrastructure such as a railway zone, steel plant, port and metros.

s: On what basis are liabilities and debt apportioned under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014?
x: Liabilities and refunds go by population ratio, assets by location and tax arrears by place of assessment.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with the basis of apportionment under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014?
o: Power — average consumption of the previous five years
x: Power was apportioned on the basis of the average consumption during the preceding five years. Assets were divided by location, liabilities by population, and tax arrears by place of assessment.

s: Where is the headquarters of the South Coast Railway, operational from 1 June 2026?
x: South Coast Railway became operational on 1 June 2026 as India's 18th railway zone, with headquarters at Visakhapatnam.

s: Which of the following pairs correctly gives the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha seats allocated to Telangana respectively?
x: Telangana was allocated 17 Lok Sabha seats and 7 Rajya Sabha seats. Andhra Pradesh was allocated 25 Lok Sabha and 11 Rajya Sabha seats.

s: How many Legislative Council seats were allocated to Telangana?
x: Telangana got 40 Council seats; AP has 58.

s: By which law was Andhra Pradesh's Legislative Council strength raised from 50 to 58?
x: The 2015 Amendment Act raised it to 58.

s: Which pair (Schedule of the AP Reorganisation Act – contents) is INCORRECTLY matched?
x: The Ninth Schedule lists PSUs and corporations; the railway zone is in the Thirteenth.

s: On what basis was power apportioned under the AP Reorganisation Act?
o: Average consumption of the previous 5 years
x: Power was shared by average consumption of the previous five years.

s: How many Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha seats respectively were allotted to Andhra Pradesh after bifurcation?
x: AP got 25 Lok Sabha and 11 Rajya Sabha seats; Telangana got 17 and 7.

s: The South Coast Railway, headquartered at Visakhapatnam, is which zone of Indian Railways?
x: The South Coast Railway is the 18th zone, operational from 1 June 2026.

s: In which year was the 32nd Constitutional Amendment enacted?
x: The 32nd Amendment was enacted in 1973, along with the Six-Point Formula. It inserted Articles 371D and 371E and came into force on 1 July 1974.

s: On which date was P.V. Narasimha Rao sworn in as Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh?
x: PVNR was sworn in on 30 Sep 1971 after Kasu Brahmananda Reddy resigned.

s: By which system were the Mulki Rules replaced after their repeal in 1973 under the Six-Point Formula?
x: The Mulki Rules were repealed in 1973 under the Six-Point Formula and replaced by the zonal system. The Telangana Regional Committee was dissolved on 1 January 1974.

s: On which date was the Telangana Regional Committee dissolved after the Six-Point Formula?
x: The TRC was dissolved on 1 January 1974.

s: Who became the Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh on 10 December 1973 after the end of President’s Rule?
x: Jalagam Vengala Rao became Chief Minister on 10 December 1973 after President’s Rule ended.

s: Who among the following spearheaded the Jai Andhra agitation as a prominent Congress leader?
x: Kakani Venkataratnam was the prominent Congress leader who spearheaded the Jai Andhra agitation. B.V. Subba Reddy was another Congress leader associated with it.

s: Why is the President's Rule imposed in Andhra Pradesh on 18 January 1973 significant?
o: the first President's Rule in the State since its formation
imposed under Article 360 for a financial emergency
the second spell of President's Rule after one in 1969
imposed to implement the Eight-Point Formula
x: After P.V. Narasimha Rao resigned on 18 January 1973 amid a breakdown of law and order during Jai Andhra, President's Rule lasted until 10 December 1973 - the first in AP since the State was formed. Article 360 concerns financial emergency; there was no President's Rule in 1969; the Eight-Point Formula (1969) is unrelated.

s: On which date did Jai Andhra protesters hoist a separate Andhra State flag?
x: The flag was hoisted on 10 December 1972, after the October 1972 Supreme Court judgment upholding the Mulki Rules.

s: On which date was the Five-Point Formula on the Mulki rules announced?
x: The Five-Point Formula came on 27 November 1972.

s: Under the Five-Point Formula, until which year were the Mulki rules to continue in the twin cities?
x: Mulki rules were to stay in the twin cities till 1977 and in Telangana till 1980.

s: How long did the President's Rule of 1973 in Andhra Pradesh last?
x: It ran from 18 January to 10 December 1973, about 11 months.

s: On which date was the Jai Andhra agitation called off?
x: After the Six-Point Formula (21 Sep 1973), the agitation was called off on 1 October 1973.

s: Which Congress leader, besides Kakani Venkataratnam, was in the Jai Andhra movement?
x: B.V. Subba Reddy was a Congress leader in the movement.

s: The Six-Point Formula of 21 September 1973 brought an end to which agitation?
x: The Jai Andhra movement ended with the Centre's Six-Point Formula and was called off on 1 October 1973.

s: Under the Five-Point Formula (1972), what share of Secretariat posts was to go to Telangana locals?
x: The Five-Point Formula gave 1 in 3 Secretariat posts to Telangana locals.

s: Under the Five-Point Formula, until which year were the Mulki rules to continue in Telangana (outside the twin cities)?
x: Mulki rules were to continue in the twin cities till 1977 and in Telangana till 1980.

s: What was the main issue of the Jai Andhra movement?
o: Andhras being treated as outsiders in Hyderabad
x: Andhras were treated as outsiders in Hyderabad, a capital built with the whole State's revenue; they demanded repeal or a separate Andhra State.

s: Through which body did the Six-Point Formula provide for backward-area development?
o: An Administrative Tribunal with zonal committees
A State Planning Commission with local sub-committees
A Central University with local sub-committees
The Telangana Regional Committee with district committees
x: Backward-area development was to be addressed through a State Planning Commission with local sub-committees.

s: What does Article 371E, associated with the Six-Point Formula, provide for?
o: Local cadres and six administrative zones
A State Planning Commission for backward areas
x: Article 371E provides for the establishment of a Central University at Hyderabad. Local cadres and zones are associated with Article 371D.

s: Articles 371D and 371E relating to Andhra Pradesh were inserted by which Constitutional Amendment?
x: The Thirty-second Amendment of 1973 gave effect to the Six-Point Formula and inserted Articles 371D and 371E.

s: Which one of the following was NOT a feature of the Six-Point Formula of 1973?
o: Continuation of the Telangana Regional Committee
Local preference in non-gazetted posts and admissions
x: The Six-Point Formula abolished the Telangana Regional Committee. It provided for a Central University at Hyderabad, an Administrative Tribunal and local preference in specified posts and admissions.

s: Under Article 371D, which body was given jurisdiction over service disputes in Andhra Pradesh?
o: The exclusive jurisdiction of the High Court
x: Article 371D provided an Administrative Tribunal for service disputes, taking them out of the High Court's jurisdiction.

s: On which date did the 32nd Constitutional Amendment come into force?
x: The 32nd Amendment came into force on 1 July 1974.

s: On which date was the Six-Point Formula, given by the Centre on 21 September 1973, approved?
x: It was approved on 18 December 1973.

s: With which Article is the Central University at Hyderabad associated?
x: The Central University is under Article 371E; Article 371D concerns local cadres and the AP Administrative Tribunal.

s: How many States and Union Territories does India have after the J&K Reorganisation of 2019 and the merger of Dadra & Nagar Haveli with Daman & Diu (January 2020)?
x: After Jammu and Kashmir ceased to be a State and became a Union Territory in 2019, India has 28 States and 8 Union Territories.

s: Under which Article can Parliament by law form a new State or alter the area, boundaries or name of a State?
x: Article 3 empowers Parliament to form new States and change their area, boundaries or names.

s: On whose recommendation can a Bill under Article 3 be introduced in Parliament?
x: It needs the President's recommendation; the State legislature's views are sought but not binding, and it passes by simple majority.

s: Which Amendment added the provision requiring the State Legislature to express its views on an Article 3 Bill within a period specified by the President?
x: The time limit for the affected State Legislature to express its views on an Article 3 Bill was added by the 5th Amendment, 1955. The 1st Amendment (1951) dealt with other matters, the 7th Amendment (1956) implemented the States reorganisation, and the 36th Amendment (1975) made Sikkim a State.

s: The Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 was enacted primarily under which Article of the Constitution of India?
x: The Act was enacted under Article 3, which empowers Parliament to form a new State out of an existing State. Article 2 deals with admission or establishment of new States.

s: Under Article 4, what is the status of a law made under Article 3?
o: An amendment needing a special majority
An amendment needing ratification by half the states
Valid only after the state legislature consents
x: Article 4 says such a law is not an amendment under Article 368.

s: By what majority does Parliament pass a Bill under Article 3?
x: An Article 3 Bill is passed by a simple majority.

s: Which Article deals with the admission or establishment of new states from outside India?
x: Article 2 covers states from outside India (e.g. Sikkim); Article 3 covers reorganisation of existing states.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Article 3 procedure:
1. The views of the affected state legislature are binding on Parliament.
2. No reference is needed for a Union Territory.
3. A fresh reference is not needed for each amendment to the Bill.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 1 is wrong: the state legislature's views are not binding.

s: Which one of the following is NOT a state of India?
x: Puducherry is a Union Territory with its own legislature under the Government of Union Territories Act, 1963.

s: Which movements mainly led to the bifurcation of Bombay State into Maharashtra and Gujarat in 1960?
o: Akali Dal and Punjabi Suba movements
x: The Samyukta Maharashtra and Mahagujarat movements led to the division of Bombay State into Maharashtra and Gujarat on 1 May 1960.

s: What status did Chandigarh get under the Punjab Reorganisation Act, 1966?
o: A Union Territory and the shared capital of Punjab and Haryana
x: The 1966 Act created Punjab and Haryana and made Chandigarh a Union Territory serving as their shared capital.

s: Which one of the following states was created in 1963 and was the first North-Eastern state to receive full statehood?
x: Nagaland became a state in 1963 and was the first North-Eastern state granted full statehood. The State of Nagaland Act was enacted in 1962.

s:
Consider the following statements about the formation of states:
1. Gujarat was formed in 1960.
2. Nagaland was formed in 1963.
3. Himachal Pradesh became a state in 1966.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Gujarat (1960) and Nagaland (1963) are right; Himachal Pradesh became a state in 1971, not 1966.

s: Manipur, Tripura and Meghalaya attained statehood in 1972 under which enactment?
x: Manipur, Tripura and Meghalaya became states in 1972 under the North-Eastern Areas (Reorganisation) Act, 1971.

s: On what grounds were the states created in 2000 mainly formed?
x: The 2000 states were created on grounds of tribal and regional backwardness, not language.

s: In which year were Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh and Uttarakhand formed?
x: The three States were formed in 2000, between AP (1956) and Telangana (2014).

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Arunachal Pradesh — State of Arunachal Pradesh Act, 1986
x: Sikkim became a state in 1975 through the 36th Constitutional Amendment. The other three pairs are correctly matched with the relevant Acts.

s:
Arrange the following states in the order of their formation:
A. Chhattisgarh
B. Uttarakhand
C. Jharkhand
D. Telangana
x: Chhattisgarh was formed on 1 November 2000, Uttarakhand on 9 November 2000, Jharkhand on 15 November 2000 and Telangana on 2 June 2014.

s: Which of the following pairs (State – basis of formation) is INCORRECTLY matched?
x: Uttarakhand was formed on grounds of regional backwardness/administration, not on a linguistic basis.

s: Who founded the Gorkha National Liberation Front and coined the term 'Gorkhaland'?
x: Subhash Ghisingh founded the GNLF in 1980 and coined the term 'Gorkhaland'.

s: After the 2019 reorganisation, which Union Territory was provided no legislature?
x: Ladakh has no legislature, while the UT of Jammu and Kashmir has a Legislative Assembly.

s: On which date did Himachal Pradesh become a full state?
x: HP became a state on 25 January 1971; in 1966 it only received Punjab's hill areas.

s: Which states were formed in 1987?
x: Mizoram, Arunachal Pradesh and Goa became states in 1987.

s: Out of which state was Nagaland, the first North-Eastern state with full statehood, carved?
x: Nagaland was carved out of Assam (State of Nagaland Act, 1962; statehood 1963).

s: The J&K Reorganisation of 2019 followed a presidential order under which Article that revoked the state's special status?
x: Special status was revoked by a presidential order under Article 370; two UTs came into being on 31 Oct 2019.

s: What happened to the 'Greater Rayalaseema' demand raised during the bifurcation of Andhra Pradesh?
o: Referred to the Srikrishna Committee for a new state
x: The Greater Rayalaseema demand was not accepted.

s: Through which measure did Sikkim become a state of India in 1975?
x: Sikkim became a state by the 36th Amendment (1975), not a 1987 Act.

s: Of the three states formed in November 2000, which was formed first?
x: Chhattisgarh (1 Nov), Uttarakhand (9 Nov), Jharkhand (15 Nov).

s: In which year was Mysore State renamed Karnataka?
x: Mysore was renamed Karnataka in 1973.

s: From which date did Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh become Union Territories?
x: Under the J&K Reorganisation Act 2019, the two UTs came into being on 31 October 2019.

s: Which body sought the separation of Darjeeling from Bengal in 1907?
x: In 1907 the Darjeeling Hillmen's Association sought separation from Bengal; the GNLF came in 1980.

s: In which year was Haryana carved out of Punjab?
x: Haryana was formed in 1966 under the Punjab Reorganisation Act 1966.

s: Which rivers constitute the principal subject of dispute between Andhra Pradesh and Telangana after bifurcation?
x: The Krishna and Godavari are the principal rivers involved in post-bifurcation water-sharing disputes between Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.

s: The objection raised by Telangana to the Polavaram–Banakacherla link is that it allegedly violates which of the following?
o: The River Boards Act and the Krishna Water Disputes Tribunal Award, 1973
The Inter-State Water Disputes Act and the Sarkaria Commission Report
The Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act and the GWDT Award, 1980
The States Reorganisation Act, 1956 and the Bachawat Commission Award
x: Telangana has argued that the link violates the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act and the Godavari Water Disputes Tribunal Award of 1980.

s:
Assertion (A): The GN Rao Committee and the BCG study formed the basis of the three-capitals plan of 2020.
Reason (R): The Sivaramakrishnan Expert Committee on the AP capital recommended a 'super capital'.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
x: A is true. R is false: the Sivaramakrishnan Committee (report August 2014) opposed a 'super capital'.

s: When did Hyderabad's period as the joint capital of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana end?
x: The ten-year joint-capital period of Hyderabad ended in June 2024.

s: With effect from which date did the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation (Amendment) Act, 2026 make Amaravati the sole, permanent capital?
x: It took effect from 2 June 2024, when Hyderabad's 10-year common-capital term ended, not 2 June 2014.

s: The number of districts in Andhra Pradesh changed in which of the following sequence between 2014 and 2025?
x: Andhra Pradesh had 13 districts in 2014, 26 in 2022 and 28 in 2025.

s: Where did the Prime Minister give the assurance of Special Category Status for Andhra Pradesh?
x: It was an assurance given by the Prime Minister in the Rajya Sabha and was not a provision of the Reorganisation Act.

s: What was the original name of the Polavaram project, proposed by Sir Shonthi Venkataramamurthy?
x: The original name was Ramapada Sagaram, proposed by Sir Shonthi Venkataramamurthy.

s: Who chaired the Expert Committee on Andhra Pradesh's new capital under Section 6?
x: K.C. Sivaramakrishnan chaired it (report Aug 2014).

s: Which Section did the AP Reorganisation (Amendment) Ordinance, 2014 amend to move Khammam submergence villages to Andhra Pradesh?
x: The Ordinance amended Section 3.

s: Who chairs the Apex Council for the Krishna and Godavari waters?
x: The Union Water Resources Minister chairs it, with both CMs.

s: On which date did the AP High Court uphold Amaravati as capital against the three-capitals plan?
x: The AP High Court upheld Amaravati on 3 March 2022.

s: On which river was Ramapada Sagaram, the original form of the Polavaram project, planned?
x: Polavaram, first proposed as Ramapada Sagaram by Sir Shonthi Venkataramamurthy, is on the Godavari.

s: How many mandals of Khammam district were transferred to Andhra Pradesh for the Polavaram project after bifurcation?
x: Seven Khammam mandals (327 revenue villages) were moved to Andhra Pradesh by the 2014 Ordinance.

s: About how many acres were pooled for Amaravati, chosen as AP's capital in 2015?
x: Amaravati was chosen in 2015 with about 33,000 acres through land pooling.

s: How many revenue villages of the seven Khammam mandals were moved to Andhra Pradesh for the Polavaram project?
x: Seven Khammam mandals with 327 revenue villages were moved to AP.

s: Which Act is the legal basis for forming new districts in Andhra Pradesh?
x: The AP Districts (Formation) Act, 1974 is the legal basis for forming new districts and altering boundaries.

s: Which of the following are among the new districts formed in Andhra Pradesh in 2025?
x: AP districts went from 26 (2022) to 28 (2025) with the new Polavaram and Markapuram districts.

s: With which provision is the AP Reorganisation (Amendment) Act, 2026 associated?
o: Abolition of the statutory concept of a state capital
Affirmation of Amaravati’s permanent statutory position as the capital
Transfer of Andhra Pradesh’s capital to Hyderabad
Recognition of Kurnool as the permanent capital of Andhra Pradesh
x: The AP Reorganisation (Amendment) Act, 2026 affirms Amaravati’s permanent statutory position as the capital of Andhra Pradesh.

s: What was the Sakala Janula Samme, associated with the separate Telangana movement?
o: An eight-point formula announced in April 1969
A parliamentary resolution adopted in July 2013
A one-day march at Tank Bund during March 2011
A general strike lasting approximately 42 days during September–October 2011
x: Sakala Janula Samme was a general strike that lasted approximately 42 days during September–October 2011. The Tank Bund march was the Million March, held in March 2011.

s: In which year was the Telangana Rashtra Samithi formed?
x: The TRS was formed in 2001, before the Centre's December 2009 announcement, the Srikrishna report (2010) and the Million March (2011).

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: 1972 — Supreme Court upheld the Mulki Rules and Jai Andhra agitation followed
x: The Srikrishna Committee submitted its report in 2010, not in 2001. The year 2001 is associated with the founding of the TRS by K. Chandrasekhar Rao.

s: Who chaired the Committee on Telangana (2010), which gave six options in its report?
x: Justice B.N. Srikrishna chaired the 2010 Committee, which reported on 30 December 2010 with six options.

s: When did the Million March at Tank Bund take place?
x: The Million March was in March 2011.

s: When was the CWC resolution for Telangana passed?
x: The CWC resolved for Telangana in July 2013.

s: On which date did the Srikrishna Committee submit its report?
x: Justice B.N. Srikrishna's committee reported on 30 December 2010 with six options.

s: When did the Centre announce the process for Telangana after K. Chandrasekhar Rao's fast?
x: The Centre's announcement came in December 2009 after KCR's fast.

s: Under the original Mulki rules of 1888, whose permission was needed to appoint an outsider to a State post?
x: The 1888 rules reserved State posts for local residents, while an outsider required the permission of the Prime Minister, or Diwan, for appointment.

s: What did the 1919 Nizam's Farman require outsiders to obtain, making the Mulki rules stricter?
o: A certificate from the Girglani Commission
The personal permission of the Nizam
The approval of the Hyderabad Legislative Council
The permission of the Prime Minister of India
x: The 1919 Farman required outsiders to obtain the Nizam's personal permission, strengthening the protection of local employment.

s: The Nizam's Mulki rules required how many years of continuous residence?
x: The Nizam's rules required 15 years' continuous residence, whereas the 1956 Gentlemen's Agreement suggested 12 years.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: The Six-Point Formula belongs to 1973. The 1985 event was the issuance of GO 610 to correct violations of the Presidential Order.

s: In which year was the Public Employment (Requirement as to Residence) Act passed?
x: The 1957 Act set a residence condition for Telangana posts.

s:
Arrange in chronological order:
1. Girglani Commission
2. GO 610
3. Jai Andhra movement
4. Six-Point Formula
x: Jai Andhra (1972) → Six-Point Formula (1973) → GO 610 (1985) → Girglani Commission (2001–04).

s: What were the stands of the Jai Telangana (1969) and Jai Andhra (1972) movements on the Mulki rules respectively?
x: Telangana in 1969 was for the Mulki rules; Andhra in 1972 was against them.

s: Of which university was Prof. K. Jayashankar, associated with the Telangana movement, a former Vice-Chancellor?
x: Prof. K. Jayashankar was a former Vice-Chancellor of Kakatiya University and was widely regarded as the ideologue of the Telangana movement.

s: The Telangana agitation of 1969 was led by which organisation, whose convener was A. Madan Mohan?
x: The 1969 Jai Telangana agitation was led by the Telangana Praja Samithi, with A. Madan Mohan as its convener.

s: Where did the Telangana agitation of 1969 begin as a student strike?
x: The agitation began as a student strike in Khammam in January 1969.

s: Who undertook the first hunger strike during the Telangana agitation of 1969?
x: The first hunger strike was undertaken by the student Ravindranath at Khammam in January 1969.

s: When was the Telangana Praja Samiti formed?
x: The Telangana Praja Samiti was formed in February 1969. It was renamed in December 1970.

s: Who was the president of the Telangana Praja Samiti?
x: Marri Channa Reddy was president of the Telangana Praja Samiti; B. Satyanarayana Reddy later led the Complete Telangana Praja Samiti.

s: The Telangana martyrs of 1969 are associated with the death of approximately how many students and agitators in police firings?
x: Severe police firings during the 1969 movement resulted in the death of over 360 students and agitators, remembered as the Telangana martyrs.

s: On which date did Prime Minister Indira Gandhi announce the Eight-Point Formula relating to Telangana?
x: The Eight-Point Formula was announced by Prime Minister Indira Gandhi at a special meeting in Delhi on 11 April 1969.

s: During which agitation did Indira Gandhi announce the Eight-Point Formula on 11 April 1969?
x: The Eight-Point Formula belongs to the Jai Telangana agitation; the Five-Point Formula of 27 November 1972 belongs to the Jai Andhra phase.

s: With whom did the Telangana Praja Samiti reach an agreement before merging with the Congress?
x: The Telangana Praja Samiti merged with the Congress after an agreement with Indira Gandhi. Those opposing the merger formed the Complete Telangana Praja Samiti under B. Satyanarayana Reddy.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Lalit Committee – Legal opinion on the validity of job safeguards
Wanchoo Committee – Official accounting of surplus funds
Bhargava Committee – Assessment of Telangana's revenue surpluses
Bhargava Committee – Legal opinion on the validity of job safeguards
x: The Bhargava Committee assessed Telangana's revenue surpluses; the Lalit Committee did the official accounting and the Wanchoo Committee examined job safeguards.

s: Who were the Chief Ministers of Andhra Pradesh during the 1969 Telangana agitation and the 1972 Jai Andhra agitation respectively?
o: P.V. Narasimha Rao and Kasu Brahmananda Reddy
Kasu Brahmananda Reddy and P.V. Narasimha Rao
Kasu Brahmananda Reddy and Jalagam Vengala Rao
Marri Channa Reddy and P.V. Narasimha Rao
x: Kasu Brahmananda Reddy was CM in 1969 and was forced to resign by the agitation; P.V. Narasimha Rao was sworn in on 30 September 1971 and was CM during Jai Andhra. Option A reverses them; Jalagam Vengala Rao became CM only on 10 December 1973; Marri Channa Reddy led the TPS and was not CM in 1969.

s: In the 1971 Lok Sabha election, the Telangana Praja Samithi won how many of the 14 seats it contested?
x: The TPS won 10 of 14 seats.

s: Under whose leadership did opponents of the TPS merger with the Congress form the Complete TPS?
x: The Complete TPS was formed under B. Satyanarayana Reddy.

s: Which pair (committee – task under the Eight-Point Formula) is correctly matched?
o: Wanchoo – Legal opinion on job safeguards
x: Wanchoo gave legal opinion on job safeguards; Bhargava examined revenue surpluses and Lalit did the official accounting.

s: Which of the following was NOT an alleged violation behind the 1969 Telangana agitation?
o: Repeal of the Mulki rules by the 32nd Amendment
Recruitment of non-locals to Telangana posts
Reclassification of local posts as state cadre
x: The 32nd Amendment came only in 1973; the others were the alleged violations behind 1969.

s: Which committee under the Eight-Point Formula examined Telangana's revenue surpluses?
x: Justice Vashist Bhargava's committee examined the revenue surpluses.

s: What was the task of the Lalit Committee (Kumar Lalit) under the Eight-Point Formula?
x: The Lalit Committee did the official accounting of the surpluses; Bhargava assessed the surpluses; Wanchoo gave legal opinion.

s: Under the Eight-Point Formula (1969), who was to review Telangana's development every six months?
x: The Eight-Point Formula provided a six-monthly review by the PM with central ministers and the Planning Commission Vice-Chairman.

s: What did the Supreme Court do in A.V.S. Narasimha Rao v. State of Andhra Pradesh, decided in 1969?
o: Struck down the Telangana residence clause of the Public Employment (Requirement as to Residence) Act, 1957
Upheld the Mulki Rules as applicable to all public posts in Andhra Pradesh
Repealed the Mulki Rules under the Six-Point Formula
x: In A.V.S. Narasimha Rao v. State of Andhra Pradesh, the Supreme Court struck down the Telangana residence requirement in the Public Employment (Requirement as to Residence) Act, 1957, invoking Article 16(3).

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Supreme Court judgment of October 1972?
o: It permitted non-locals to be barred from public posts in Hyderabad and Telangana.
It concerned the residence clause of the 1957 Public Employment Act.
It immediately contributed to the Jai Andhra Movement.
x: The 1972 ruling concerned the older Mulki Rules; the 1957 Act's residence clause had been struck down in 1969.

s: Under Article 16(3), who can prescribe residence requirements for public employment?
x: Article 16(3) empowers only Parliament; Article 371D is a special route for Andhra Pradesh.

s: Which case of October 1972 upheld the old Mulki Rules as valid and in force?
o: A.V.S. Narasimha Rao v. State of AP
Director of Industries v. V. Venkata Reddy
Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala
x: Director of Industries v. V. Venkata Reddy (Oct 1972) upheld the Mulki Rules and triggered Jai Andhra.

s: The one-man Girglani Commission examined violations of GO 610 and which other order?
x: J.M. Girglani examined violations of GO 610 and the 1975 Presidential Order, finding many non-local appointments, especially in Zone VI.

s: After the reorganisation of Andhra Pradesh in 2014, which zones of the undivided State were retained by Andhra Pradesh for its 13 districts?
x: After 2014, Andhra Pradesh retained Zones I to IV for its 13 districts; Zones V and VI related to the Telangana region.

s: Why was GO 610 issued?
o: Introduce the Mulki rules in Hyderabad State
Repatriate non-local employees appointed in violation of the Presidential Order and restore posts to Telangana locals
Create six local zones for the first time
x: GO 610 sought to repatriate non-local employees appointed contrary to the 1975 Presidential Order and restore local posts to Telangana candidates.

s: Which government issued GO 610 (30 December 1985) to repatriate non-locals appointed in violation of the 1975 Presidential Order?
x: GO 610 was issued by the NTR (TDP) government; the Girglani Commission (2001) was set up by the Chandrababu Naidu government.

s: In which Zone was Hyderabad included under the 1975 zonal system of undivided Andhra Pradesh?
x: Hyderabad was in Zone VI; Zones I-III were Coastal Andhra, Zone IV Rayalaseema and Zones V-VI Telangana.

s: Which districts formed Zone II under the 1975 Presidential Order?
o: East Godavari, West Godavari and Krishna
x: Zone II was East Godavari, West Godavari and Krishna; Zone IV was Rayalaseema and Zone VI included Hyderabad.

s: Which government set up the Girglani Commission in 2001?
x: Naidu set it up in 2001; GO 610 was NTR's (1985).

s: In which zone did the Girglani Commission find large-scale violations?
x: Its 2004 report found large-scale violations, especially in Zone VI.

s: How many zones and multi-zones does Andhra Pradesh have under the AP Public Employment Order-2025?
x: The 2025 Order provides 6 zones and 2 multi-zones.

s: Which of the following districts was NOT in Zone VI under the 1975 Presidential Order?
x: Zone VI had Hyderabad, Ranga Reddy, Nizamabad, Mahbubnagar, Medak and Nalgonda.

s: In which year did the Girglani Commission submit its report?
x: Set up in 2001, the one-man Girglani Commission reported in 2004.

s: Which of the following tribal communities were associated with the Srikakulam Girijan struggle?
x: The principal tribal communities associated with the struggle were the Savaras, also called Soras, and the Jatapus.

s: Who led the Srikakulam Girijan struggle?
o: Tarimela Nagi Reddy and Chandra Pulla Reddy
x: The school teachers Vempatapu Satyam and Adibhatla Kailasam led the Srikakulam struggle; Majumdar and Sanyal led Naxalbari.

s: The Srikakulam Girijan struggle began under which party?
x: The struggle began under the CPI(M) and shifted to the CPI(ML) only in 1969.

s: At which place were two tribal activists killed on 31 October 1967, triggering the Srikakulam struggle?
x: Koraana and Manganna were killed at Levidi on the way to a Girijan Sangham meeting.

s: During which period did the Srikakulam Girijan struggle take place?
x: The Srikakulam Girijan struggle ran from 1968 to 1970; 1967 is the year of Naxalbari.

s: In which year were Vempatapu Satyam and Adibhatla Kailasam, leaders of the Srikakulam Girijan struggle, killed?
x: Both leaders were killed in July 1970, and the struggle broke up by the end of 1970.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Srikakulam Girijan struggle:
1. It began under the CPI(M).
2. It shifted to the CPI(ML) in 1969.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The struggle began under the CPI(M) and moved to the CPI(ML) when that party was formed in 1969.

s: Which slogan was associated with the Naxalbari uprising?
x: “Land to the tiller” was the slogan associated with the Naxalbari peasant uprising.

s: Who led the Naxalbari peasant uprising of March–May 1967?
o: Tarimela Nagi Reddy and Chandra Pulla Reddy
x: Charu Majumdar and Kanu Sanyal led the Naxalbari uprising in Darjeeling district. Nagi Reddy, Pulla Reddy, Venkaiah and Patnaik led the 1967 Andhra extremist wing; Kondapalli Seetharamaiah founded the PWG in 1980; Vempatapu Satyam is linked with Srikakulam.

s: What did the expression "Ballot to Bullet" reject?
o: The Chinese model of guerrilla warfare
x: The “Ballot to Bullet” line rejected the CPI(M)’s parliamentary path and favoured armed revolutionary struggle.

s: The Naxalbari uprising of 1967 took place in which district of West Bengal?
x: Naxalbari lies in the Siliguri sub-division of Darjeeling district, West Bengal.

s: Who among the following led the extremist wing that split from the CPI(M) in Andhra Pradesh in 1967?
o: Tarimela Nagi Reddy and Chandra Pulla Reddy
B. Narsinga Rao and Sri Sri
x: The 1967 Andhra extremist wing was led by Tarimela Nagi Reddy, Chandra Pulla Reddy, Kolla Venkaiah and Nagabhushana Patnaik.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: AP extremist CPI(ML) wing – Merger of PWG and MCC
CPI (Maoist) – Charu Majumdar with Kanu Sanyal
x: The PWG was founded by Kondapalli Seetharamaiah; CPI(ML) is linked to Charu Majumdar and Kanu Sanyal, and CPI (Maoist) to the PWG–MCC merger.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Naxalite groups?
o: The AP extremist CPI(ML) wing dates to 1967.
People's War Group was formed in 1980.
x: CPI (Maoist) was formed in 2004, not 1992; the other three dates are correct.

s: In which year was the CPI(ML) formed?
x: The CPI(ML) was formed in 1969, viewed India as semi-feudal and followed the Chinese-model protracted guerrilla war.

s: The CPI (Maoist) was formed in 2004 by the merger of which groups?
x: CPI (Maoist) was formed in 2004 by the merger of the People's War Group and the MCC.

s:
Consider the following statements about the CPI(ML):
1. It was founded in 1969 by Charu Majumdar.
2. Its base was West Bengal.
3. It saw the Indian state as semi-feudal and followed a Chinese-model protracted guerrilla war.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: All three are correct: CPI(ML) was formed in 1969 by Charu Majumdar, based in West Bengal, on a Chinese-model guerrilla line.

s: Who founded the People's War Group in 1980?
x: Kondapalli Seetharamaiah founded the PWG in 1980; Charu Majumdar founded the CPI(ML) in 1969.

s: In which year was the Maoist leader Kishanji killed by security forces?
x: Kishanji, a top Maoist leader, was killed by security forces in 2011.

s: In which year was the People's War Group (PWG) banned in Andhra Pradesh?
x: The PWG was banned in Andhra Pradesh in 1992.

s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
x: The Greyhounds were raised in 1989; 1992 is the year the PWG was banned.

s: What did the Bhargava Commission, set up in 1977, inquire into?
o: The reorganisation of Andhra Pradesh districts
Alleged encounter killings of Naxalite cadres in Andhra Pradesh
The procurement activities of the Girijan Cooperative Corporation
x: The Bhargava Commission, headed by Justice Vashist Bhargava, was set up in 1977 to inquire into alleged encounter killings during the Emergency.

s: Who headed the 1977 commission that inquired into Emergency 'encounter' killings of Naxalites in Andhra Pradesh?
x: The Bhargava Commission (1977) was headed by Justice Vashist Bhargava.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Bhargava Commission?
o: It was headed by Justice Vashist Bhargava.
It inquired into the implementation of land reforms.
It probed encounter killings during the Emergency (1975–77).
x: The Bhargava Commission probed Emergency encounter killings, not land reforms.

s: Which of the following raised the Greyhounds, an elite anti-Naxal force, in 1989?
x: Greyhounds is an elite anti-Naxal special police force of the Andhra Pradesh Police, raised in 1989.

s: Government–Maoist peace talks were held in Hyderabad in October 2004 during the tenure of which government?
x: Government–Maoist talks were held in Hyderabad in October 2004 during the YSR government.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Greyhounds base at Anandapuram:
1. It secures the Left Wing Extremism corridor of the Alluri Sitharama Raju and Parvathipuram Manyam districts.
2. These districts lie in north coastal Andhra Pradesh.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The Anandapuram base secures the LWE corridor of the ASR and Parvathipuram Manyam districts, both in north coastal Andhra Pradesh.

s: During which period did over 1,200 Naxalite cadres surrender in Andhra Pradesh under the surrender policy?
x: Under DGP H.J. Dora, the surrender policy of 1998–2001 saw over 1,200 cadres surrender.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Greyhounds?
o: It is an elite anti-Naxal special police force.
Its training centre is at Anandapuram.
It is a dog squad of the AP Police.
x: The Greyhounds is a special police force, not a dog squad.

s: Where is the Greyhounds Training Centre of Andhra Pradesh located?
x: The Greyhounds Training Centre is at Anandapuram near Visakhapatnam, under Section 9 of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014.

s: Under which Director General of Police did over 1,200 Naxalite cadres surrender in Andhra Pradesh during 1998–2001?
x: The surrender policy of 1998–2001 ran under DGP H.J. Dora (1996–2002).

s: Under which Act was the Greyhounds Training Centre at Anandapuram set up for Andhra Pradesh?
x: The Greyhounds Training Centre at Anandapuram comes under Section 9 of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014.

s: On which date was the Revolutionary Writers' Association (Virasam) founded?
x: Virasam was founded on 4 July 1970 in Hyderabad.

s: Where was the first meeting of Virasam held in 1970?
x: The first Virasam meeting was held at Khammam in 1970.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Revolutionary Writers' Association (Virasam):
1. Sri Sri was its founding president.
2. Kodavatiganti Kutumba Rao and Rachakonda Viswanatha Sastry were its vice-presidents.
3. Gaddar was one of its founding vice-presidents.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Sri Sri was president and Kutumba Rao and Viswanatha Sastry were vice-presidents; Gaddar was with Art Lovers / Jana Natya Mandali, not a Virasam vice-president.

s: Besides Virasam, the Srikakulam movement reshaped Telugu culture through which troupe?
x: Srikakulam made AP a core base of Indian Maoism and influenced Telugu literature through Virasam and Jana Natya Mandali.

s: Which was the first poetry collection of Virasam, published in 1970?
x: Jhamjha (1970) was Virasam's first poetry collection.

s: In which year was Art Lovers, founded in 1970 by B. Narsinga Rao and Gaddar, renamed Jana Natya Mandali?
x: Art Lovers (1970) became Jana Natya Mandali in 1971.

s: Who were the founding vice-presidents of Virasam?
o: Kodavatiganti Kutumba Rao and Rachakonda Viswanatha Sastry
Sri Sri and Kodavatiganti Kutumba Rao
x: Kodavatiganti Kutumba Rao and Rachakonda Viswanatha Sastry were the founding vice-presidents; Sri Sri was president.

s: At whose 60th-birthday celebrations in 1970 did Andhra University students issue the pamphlet that led to the founding of Virasam?
x: Virasam grew out of a pamphlet by Andhra University students at Sri Sri's 60th-birthday celebrations in Visakhapatnam (February 1970).

s: In which city was the Revolutionary Writers' Association (Virasam) founded on 4 July 1970?
x: Virasam was founded at Hyderabad on 4 July 1970; its first meeting was later held at Khammam.

s: What does the Girijan Cooperative Corporation, headquartered at Visakhapatnam, mainly do?
o: Procures minor forest produce and supplies essentials to tribals
x: The GCC procures minor forest produce and supplies essential goods, freeing tribals from moneylenders.

s: From which Plan were Integrated Tribal Development Agencies (ITDAs) set up under the Tribal Sub-Plan?
x: ITDAs were set up under the Tribal Sub-Plan from the Fifth Plan, beginning in 1974–75.

s: The AP Scheduled Areas Land Transfer Regulation was tightened in 1970 (Regulation 1 of 1970) mainly to
o: stop land in Scheduled Areas passing from tribals to non-tribals
set up Integrated Tribal Development Agencies
allow procurement of minor forest produce by the GCC
abolish zamindari in the Srikakulam Agency
x: Regulation 1 of 1970, a response to the tribal unrest, barred transfer of land in Scheduled Areas from tribals to non-tribals. ITDAs came under the Tribal Sub-Plan from the Fifth Plan (1974-75); minor forest produce procurement is the Girijan Cooperative Corporation's work; zamindari abolition was not the Regulation's purpose.

s: The Anti-arrack movement is regarded as one of India’s most successful movements led by which group?
x: The anti-arrack movement began in 1992 at Dubagunta village in Nellore district, led by rural women. It is regarded as one of India's most successful women-led movements.

s: The anti-arrack agitation of 1991 emerged primarily from discussions held in which programme?
o: Workers' education classes under the Kisan Sabha
x: Women discussed the effects of men's arrack drinking during Aksharajyothi adult-literacy classes, which helped initiate the agitation.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about prohibition in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Total prohibition came before the ban on arrack.
x: Arrack was banned first (1 October 1993); total prohibition followed in 1995 and was lifted in 1997.

s: Which of the following pairs relating to the Anti-arrack movement is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Legislative elections – main method of the movement
Broomsticks and chilli powder – used by women protesters
x: Women closed shops and stopped auctions using broomsticks and chilli powder; legislative elections were not a method of the movement.

s: Dubagunta, where the anti-arrack movement began, is in which district?
x: Dubagunta village is in Nellore district, not Guntur.

s: Which of the following was NOT a method of the anti-arrack women?
x: Legislative elections were not a method; women closed shops and stopped auctions with broomsticks and chilli powder.

s: In which region did Kallur Subbarao lead anti-liquor and Swadeshi movements in the 1930s?
x: Kallur Subbarao led the anti-liquor and Swadeshi movements in the Dattamandalas (Rayalaseema).

s: Who led the anti-arrack movement that began in Dubagunta village of Nellore district?
x: The anti-arrack movement of rural women at Dubagunta was led by Vardhineni (Dubagunta) Rosamma.

s: From which date was arrack prohibited in Andhra Pradesh after the anti-arrack movement?
x: Arrack was prohibited in AP from 1 October 1993; total prohibition came in 1995 and was lifted in 1997.

s: Which of the following commissions was chaired by Kaka Kalelkar?
x: Kaka Kalelkar chaired the First Backward Classes Commission, set up in January 1953 under Article 340; it reported in 1955. The Second Commission was chaired by B.P. Mandal.

s: Which was the first Andhra Pradesh Backward Class Commission, which grouped BCs into A–D categories?
x: The Anantharaman Commission (1968–70) was the first AP Backward Class Commission and grouped BCs into A–D categories.

s: Which of the following was the task of the Muralidhar Rao Commission?
o: It introduced the A–B–C–D categorisation of Scheduled Castes.
It examined whether minorities were included in the Backward Class list.
It imposed prohibition throughout Andhra Pradesh.
It conducted the first national survey of OBC population.
x: The Muralidhar Rao Commission examined whether minorities were included in the Backward Class list.

s: What percentage of OBC reservation did the Mandal Commission recommend?
x: The Mandal Commission recommended 27% reservation for OBCs.

s: The government of which Prime Minister implemented the Mandal Commission recommendations on 7 August 1990?
x: V.P. Singh's government implemented the Mandal recommendations on 7 August 1990.

s: Under which Article was the First Backward Classes Commission (Kaka Kalelkar) set up in January 1953?
x: The Kaka Kalelkar Commission was set up under Article 340 in January 1953.

s: In which year did the Muralidhar Rao Commission on backward classes in Andhra Pradesh take charge?
x: The Muralidhar Rao Commission took charge on 27 January 1982; Anantharaman (1968–70) was the first AP BC Commission.

s: In which year was the Second Backward Classes Commission under B.P. Mandal set up?
x: The Mandal Commission was set up on 1 January 1979; it reported in 1980 and was implemented in 1990.

s: During which years did the Anantharaman Commission, the first Andhra Pradesh Backward Class Commission, work?
x: The Anantharaman Commission (1968–70) was the first AP BC Commission and grouped BCs into A–D.

s: In which year did the Mandal Commission submit its report?
x: The Mandal Commission, set up on 1 January 1979, submitted its report on 31 December 1980.

s: In which year did the First Backward Classes Commission under Kaka Kalelkar submit its report?
x: The Kalelkar Commission was set up in January 1953 and reported in 1955.

s: What share of the population did the Muralidhar Rao Commission arrive at by combining BC, ST and religious-group populations?
x: The Muralidhar Rao Commission combined these populations as 29.08%, which led to a big rise in the State's reservation quota.

s: Where was Kusuma Dharmanna's Adi-Andhra Mahasabha of 1936 held?
x: The 1936 Mahasabha was at Vizianagaram; Bhagya Reddy Varma's 1919 conference was at Machilipatnam.

s: Which of the following movements inspired the Adi-Andhra leaders in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Bhu Poratam and Power Tariff Agitation
x: Phule’s Satyashodhak Samaj, founded in 1873, and Periyar’s Self-Respect Movement influenced the Adi-Andhra leaders.

s: Who led the 1919 Adi-Andhra conference at Machilipatnam?
x: Bhagya Reddy Varma led the 1919 Machilipatnam conference; Kusuma Dharmanna led the 1936 Vizianagaram Mahasabha.

s: In which year was Phule's Satyashodhak Samaj, which inspired the Adi-Andhra leaders, founded?
x: Jyotirao Phule's Satyashodhak Samaj was founded in 1873.

s: The Karamchedu massacre of Dalits took place in which district?
x: The Karamchedu massacre occurred in Prakasam district on 17 July 1985.

s: The Chunduru massacre occurred on 6 August 1991 in which district?
x: The Chunduru massacre occurred on 6 August 1991 in Guntur district.

s: Which of the following developments followed the Karamchedu incident?
o: Dalits formed independent Dalit Mahasabhas after breaking away from Congress and Communist parties.
Total prohibition was imposed across Andhra Pradesh.
The Mandal Commission was immediately constituted.
The MRPS was founded at Eedumudi.
x: After Karamchedu, Dalits broke away from the Congress and Communist parties and formed independent Dalit Mahasabhas.

s: In which year did the Karamchedu massacre of Dalits take place?
x: Karamchedu was on 17 July 1985; 1991 is the year of the Chunduru massacre.

s: Karamchedu, the site of the 1985 massacre of Dalits, now lies in which district?
x: Karamchedu was in Prakasam district in 1985 and is now in Bapatla district.

s: Who founded the Andhra Pradesh Dalit Mahasabha in 1985, after Karamchedu?
x: Katti Padmarao is identified as its founder, with Bojja Tarakam also recognised as a founder.

s: Besides Katti Padmarao, who is recognised as a founder of the AP Dalit Mahasabha?
x: Bojja Tarakam is also recognised as a founder of the AP Dalit Mahasabha (1985).

s: Who founded the Madiga Reservation Porata Samiti (Madiga Dandora)?
x: Manda Krishna Madiga was the founder-president of the MRPS.

s: What was the main demand of the Madiga Dandora?
o: Inclusion of minorities in the BC list
x: MRPS demanded sub-categorisation of SC reservation so that Madigas get a fair share.

s:
Consider the following statements about the MRPS:

x: All are correct: MRPS was founded on 7 July 1994 at Eedumudi, Prakasam; Manda Krishna Madiga got the Padma Shri in 2025.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about N.G. Ranga and the peasant movement?
o: Ranga founded the Indian Peasants' Institute in 1933.
The Institute was located at Nidubrolu.
Ranga was a founder of the All India Kisan Sabha in 1936.
The All India Kisan Sabha was a mass organisation of the Congress.

s: The power tariff agitation of 2000 was directed against which issue?
o: Auction of arrack shops under prohibition policy
Hikes in electricity tariffs under power-sector reforms
x: Left parties and farmers protested electricity tariff hikes introduced under power-sector reforms during the 2000 agitation.

s: In which year did the Bashir Bagh firing on power-tariff protesters in Hyderabad take place?
x: The Bashir Bagh firing was on 28 August 2000, during the power tariff agitation.

s: Where did N.G. Ranga found the Indian Peasants' Institute in 1933?
x: N.G. Ranga set up the Indian Peasants' Institute at Nidubrolu in 1933.

s: The All India Kisan Sabha is a mass organisation of which party?
x: The All India Kisan Sabha (founded 1936 at Lucknow) became a mass organisation of the CPI, not the Congress. (After the 1964 split a CPI(M)-aligned AIKS also exists, so CPI(M) is not offered as an option.)

s:
Consider the following statements about Bhu Poratam:
1. It was jointly launched by the CPI and CPI(M) in Andhra Pradesh.
2. It was launched in 1997.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Bhu Poratam was a joint CPI–CPI(M) land struggle, but it was launched in 2007, not 1997.

s: The principal objective of Bhu Poratam was to occupy and distribute which land to the landless?
x: Bhu Poratam sought the occupation and distribution of government and surplus land to landless people.
